blocks.text: Nordic wonder and an ancient art – readers’ best photographs
Click here to submit a picture for publication in these online galleries and/or on the Guardian letters page

blocks.alt: Toma, Hokkaido, Japan ‘For a brief period in May, before the rice planting begins, the vast fields of Toma are filled with water. As the sun dipped, a dramatic shaft of light pierced across these seasonal paddies – capturing a fleeting harmony between ancient Japanese agriculture and the raw power of the landscape.’
North Sulawesi, Indonesia ‘A crested black macaque. These macaques are completely unafraid of humans, allowing me to take close-up portraits.’
Kaohsiung City, Taiwan ‘Residents of the Guomao community observe the National Day of the Republic of China with decorative flags.’
Colorado, US ‘I planted sunflowers in my backyard specifically to attract seed-eating birds. This American goldfinch is enjoying his free lunch with a seed in his beak.’

London, UK ‘Autumn is creeping into our north London garden, and one of this summer’s fox kits is now almost fully grown. We’ve named her Selina. She still patrols the paving, investigates anything that might be edible, and keeps a close eye on the humans. She may be losing the look of a kit, but not the attitude.’
Trondheim, Norway ‘An early morning in September. I was standing on the bridge over the Nidelva River.’
Tappenkarsee, Austria ‘The still water of the lake while out hiking in early autumn.’

Wisconsin, US ‘I was photographing a bee dancing between flowers when I spied a praying mantis doing the same. With a quick snatch, the bee was imprisoned; taken for lunch. I continued photographing in awe until I realised how intruding I was.’
Arizona, US ‘A freight train passing over a small trestle bridge. Shot near Kingman.’
New Jersey, US ‘The flower shows a moment of getting separated that captured my attention. A broken beauty.’

Old Cairo, Egypt ‘This photo is from the famous “Street of the Tentmakers” in historic Cairo, one of the few places where the ancient art of appliqué (khayamiya) still survives. I found this craftsman, a patriarch of his trade, working in the same spot he has for decades. His focused concentration and weathered hands tell the story of a lifetime dedicated to preserving a cultural heritage.’
Lago di Bolsena, Italy ‘Taken just after sunset, trying to capture the different colours reflecting from the ripples in the lake water.’
Thuringia, Germany ‘My wife and a friend descending the maximally minimalist staircase in the Bauhaus museum in Weimar designed by Heike Hanada.’

Skaneateles, NY, US ‘On the root ball of an overturned tree grew a mass of honey mushrooms (Armillaria mellea) alongside and atop pincushion moss (Leucobryum glaucum) and its spore capsules. The fungi and the mosses share a symbiotic relationship allowing both to flourish and propagate.’
